questions.q: What problem does a managed identity actually solve?
options: It eliminates the need to store and rotate credentials directly in a linked service
It makes pipelines run faster
It replaces the need for any Azure RBAC role assignments
It only works for SQL Server connections
questions.explain: A managed identity gives Data Factory its own Microsoft Entra identity, so other services can grant that identity access directly — no credential ever needs to be stored in the factory's definition.

questions.q: What happens to a system-assigned managed identity when its data factory is deleted?
options: Azure automatically deletes the identity along with the factory
The identity persists indefinitely and must be manually deleted
The identity transfers automatically to a new factory
System-assigned identities can never be deleted
questions.explain: A system-assigned managed identity is tied directly to its resource's lifecycle — when the factory is deleted, Azure deletes the identity with it.

questions.q: How does a user-assigned managed identity differ from a system-assigned one?
options: It's a standalone resource that can be shared across multiple data factories and survives if one factory is deleted
It can only be used by exactly one activity at a time
It requires no role assignments at all
It's automatically created for every data factory with no option to disable it
questions.explain: A user-assigned managed identity exists as its own Azure resource, independent of any single factory's lifecycle, making it useful when several factories need to share the same identity and permissions.

questions.q: What must you do before a data factory's managed identity can access a Key Vault's secrets?
options: Grant the identity Get and List permissions on the vault's secrets
Nothing — access is automatic once both resources exist in the same subscription
Manually copy the secret value into the linked service first
Delete and recreate the Key Vault
questions.explain: The managed identity needs to be explicitly granted Get and List permissions (via access policy or role assignment) before any linked service using that identity can retrieve secrets from the vault.

questions.q: In the AzureKeyVaultSecret JSON pattern, what does the linked service actually store?
options: Only a reference to the secret's name and the Key Vault linked service — never the actual value
The full plaintext password, base64-encoded
An encrypted copy of the password within the same JSON
Nothing — the field must be left completely empty
questions.explain: The linked service definition holds only secretName and a reference to the Key Vault linked service (store) — Data Factory fetches the real value at runtime, never storing it in the definition itself.
